Pendulum squat.The mechanics, explained

200 KG · 20 REPS
QuadricepsGlutes

▼

What do you do?

Model. This is a side-view model with rigid bones and slow movement. The feet stay fixed on the platform and the hip stays against the backrest, which rotates with the machine arm. Muscle demand is estimated from the torque around each joint: force × moment arm, including the weight of your legs.

Machine. Geometry estimated from photographs and specifications of a Gymleco 045 (initial resistance of 23 kg at the top and 17 kg at the bottom). With 20 kg per side, the shoulder load is about 80 kg; your legs also move your torso and thighs.

Muscles. “Glutes” represents all hip extensors; the hamstrings also contribute. Calves and other muscles are omitted for simplicity.

Blue. Blue shows torso support. The shoulder pads and belt turn blue according to pressure. Blue arrows show where you push: up against the shoulder pads and back against the backrest at the point of contact. The black belt arrow shows your abdomen pressing into it. The backrest can only push against your back, so glute emphasis has a limit without a belt. The belt engages when needed; the Belt button lets you keep it on or off.

Pivot. The orange arrow grows thicker as the required force increases. When the line of force approaches the pivot, its moment arm appears in grey: the shorter it is, the more force is needed for the same load.

Scope. This model illustrates trends; it does not measure an individual person.
